source.title: Inference Compute-Optimal Video Vision Language Models
source.authors: Pei-Qi Wang; ShengYun Peng; Xuewen Zhang; Han-Chao Yu; Yi-Bo Yang; Lifu Huang; Fujun Liu; Qifan Wang

record.tranche_reason: The study measures scaling and fit-based prediction in video VLM fine-tuning, and finds that predictive quality varies by task and fitting choices. This refines the scope of scaling-law claims rather than testing language-model pretraining loss.
record.gate_note: The paper reports downstream video-task performance, not held-out pretraining cross-entropy. It compares parametric fits and tests extrapolation from the star sweep to the isoFLOP sweep. Cited results from other studies are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: New setting: fine-tuned video VLMs (Llama-3.2 1B/2.8B/7.5B). The study fits power laws of downstream task error against LM size, frames, tokens per frame and fine-tuning data size, then checks fit quality and extrapolation from the star sweep to the isoFLOP sweep. This bears on V5 (fine-tuning regime), V6 (downstream predictability) and V7 (fit-form and fitting-procedure dependence). It does not measure pretraining loss, so T3 fits better than T5.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that a bagged additive power law with data interaction terms models average video-task performance well, and use it to derive an inference-compute-optimal frontier. The frontier requires jointly scaling LM size, frames and tokens per frame. Allocation is task-specific, and more fine-tuning data shifts the frontier toward smaller LMs and more frames and tokens. They note per-task extrapolation is weak for some tasks.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses fine-tuned video VLMs, downstream task metrics, and inference-compute sweeps, rather than language-model pretraining cross-entropy and training-compute scaling.
record.method_sensitivity: Task affects extrapolation quality; parametric fit form, bootstrap aggregation method and number of resamples, parameter initialization, exponent positivity constraints, loss function, and log-space computation affect fit quality. The paper also reports that data size changes the predicted inference-compute frontier.

fits_no_version.finding: The inference-compute-optimal frontier requires jointly scaling LM size, frames and tokens per frame. As fine-tuning data grows, the optimal LM size shrinks and frames/tokens grow (elasticities eN≈-0.22, eT≈0.17, eV≈0.79).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Inference-compute-optimal allocation in fine-tuned VLMs follows stable power-like trends that shift with fine-tuning data size.

fits_no_version.finding: The utility of scaling factors, and hence the optimal allocation, varies strongly across video tasks.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Compute-optimal allocation is task-specific for downstream metrics.

record.peer_reviewed: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
record.problems: The authors report high variability in fitted parameters with about 100 examples, task-specific extrapolation failures, and limits on generalization to much higher inference compute. Only three language-model sizes are tested, and the paper notes that the family lacks sizes between 8B and 70B. The study evaluates downstream task metrics rather than pretraining loss.
record.rows_left_out: The paper reports additional task-specific frontiers and sweep results mainly in Figures 8–10, but the supplied text does not give their numerical values and the main reported findings are captured in r1 and r7–r8. Table 8 and parts of Table 9 are flattened; unclear individual cells were not assigned.

untested.parts: Held-out LM pretraining loss versus parameters, tokens or compute.

Extrapolation to runs orders of magnitude larger. Star→IsoFLOP extrapolates within about 2 orders of inference compute, mostly to cheaper runs; the authors say generalization to 10x compute is uncertain.
Training-compute-optimal parameter/token allocation. The study optimizes inference compute only.
Image or video pretraining, repeated data, and transfer. Only video-instruction fine-tuning with task error as the measure is tested.
Prediction from pretraining loss; LM sizes beyond 7.5B.
Parameter counting, training schedule, and disagreement among published LM laws.

missing.what: Table 8 ablation numbers. Without log-space computation, Star→IsoFLOP E% 2.93 and R2 -0.62, versus 1.33 and 0.92 with it. Positivity bound and init variants (zero init CV MSE 0.43, r(500) 0.2) also differ.
High bootstrap variability of fitted exponents and coefficients with about 100 runs.
In-distribution CV metrics for mult/add/add-interacts (e.g. mult CV MSE 1.21, E% 6.73, R2 0.88).

record.verdict_notes: The measure is downstream task error after fine-tuning, not pretraining loss. The scaling axes include inference-time factors (frames, tokens per frame), so V5/V6 support holds only in this setting. Only three LM sizes were tested. Table 2 S→I MSE for add-interact (0.77) differs from Table 9 (0.95) for the presumably same configuration; this is unexplained in the text.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out language-model pretraining loss as a function of parameters, tokens, or training compute.
Prediction of pretraining loss on much larger language-model runs from small runs; its extrapolation target is downstream video-task performance.
Training-compute-optimal language-model parameter/token allocation and stable power-law growth with training compute; the study optimizes video VLM inference compute instead.
Effects of depth, width, and other architecture details at fixed parameter count.
Other modalities, repeated-data training, and transfer beyond the tested video VLM fine-tuning setting.
Prediction from pretraining loss and performance beyond the tested video downstream tasks and model configurations.
Parameter-counting choices, training-schedule variation, data variation beyond the tested fine-tuning sizes, and disagreement between published language-model pretraining laws.

rows.operation_detail: Ablate parameter-fitting procedures, including initialization, constraints, and computation in log space.

conditions.value: initialization, positivity constraints on exponents, log-space computation, and loss function

rows.value: The paper reports that 500 random initializations are used to mitigate poor local minima, positivity constraints on exponents degrade performance, log-space computation improves performance across metrics, and MSE outperforms Huber loss.
rows.note: This records the paper's explicit qualitative summary; table values are not assigned because the flattened layout is unclear.

relationships.reason: Performance improves with diminishing returns in each factor and data size (r1). Additive power law with interactions fits with CV R2 0.98 (r2) and Star→IsoFLOP R2 0.92, E% 1.33 (r3).
relationships.display_finding: Error improved with diminishing returns, and an additive power law with interactions achieved cross-validation R² of 0.98 and Star-to-IsoFLOP R² of 0.92 with 1.33% error.
